insight: For Ghana, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally been a positive turning point, with the team gaining momentum in 6 out of 8 breaks, indicating a slight increase in performance after the brief pause. However, when Ghana was pressing before a hydration break, they tended to lose momentum, with a significant average decline of 0.300 minutes, and were unable to regain it after the break. In contrast, when Ghana was not pressing before a break, they were able to maintain or slightly increase their momentum, with an average increase of 0.083 minutes, suggesting that the team is better able to refocus and recharge when not under intense pressure. Overall, these statistics suggest that Ghana benefits from hydration breaks, but needs to adjust its strategy when pressing to avoid losing momentum during the pause.
